title: Thesios: Synthesizing Accurate Counterfactual I/O Traces from I/O Samples
problem: Accurate synthesis of full-resolution I/O traces from down-sampled traces across multiple disks and storage servers is needed to enable counterfactual what-if analyses without costly production experiments.
motivation: Representative modeling of I/O activity is crucial for designing large-scale distributed storage systems and assessing the impact of hypothetical new policies and hardware before deployment.
method: Thesios carefully combines down-sampled I/O traces from multiple disks attached to multiple storage servers to synthesize full-resolution traces. The approach reconstructs representative traces that match actual disk metrics with high accuracy, enabling counterfactual analyses of policy changes, hardware modifications, and system configuration adjustments.
key_novelty: Accurate synthesis of full-resolution I/O traces from down-sampled samples across multiple sources enables efficient counterfactual analysis without production experiments.
contributions: A methodology for synthesizing accurate full-resolution I/O traces from down-sampled traces across multiple disks and servers
Achieves 95-99.5% accuracy in read/write requests, 90-97% in utilization, and 80-99.8% in read latency compared to actual measurements
Enables diverse counterfactual analyses including disk capacity/utilization, data placement policies, RPM reduction, and buffer cache sizing
Eliminates need for costly and risky A/B experiments in production for evaluating hypothetical storage system changes
primary_theme: I/O trace synthesis for storage system analysis
